issue.body:
Can timeout and scheduling changes recover complete positive control pairs without repairing tasks? Follow-up to #28; investigation remains open.

**Completed controls:** four existing Matchms exports have positive nop/oracle pairs, preserved regression tests and clean oracle commands; all 40 task files are unchanged. These are completed controls, not new exports. [Results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/188091eb/experiments/29-runtime-limits/matchms-control-results.json).

**OpenMS:** the original 60-second checkout timed out again; the 300-second arm completed the same commit in 77.9 seconds with no tracked changes, using the same CPU/memory limits. This establishes acquisition recovery only. Bootstrap, PR discovery and task generation were not run. Both containers were removed and the archive verified. [Evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/875eab80/experiments/29-runtime-limits/openms-checkout-readback-001.json).

**Scanpy:** all 16 recorded bootstrap commands replayed with original exits and no repairs, crossing the saved Dockerfile's stop-at-first-failure barrier. Smoke/fresh-image checks remain false. The unchanged PR4389 export's nop/oracle controls are running at 300 versus 1,200 verifier seconds. Results remain pending. [Protocol](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/65cfc8b5/experiments/29-runtime-limits/scanpy-controls-protocol.md).

**Remaining:** verify Scanpy controls and cleanup; assess faithful OHIF reconstruction; checkpoint MMseqs2's bootstrap comparison and model allowance. Longer verifier limits cannot resolve installation or checkout failures.

**Budget and retention:** nine terminal jobs used 1.18825 allocated CPU-hours. Active Scanpy controls permit at most 9.6667 more within the existing 32-hour ceiling, on reserved capacity. Zero model calls. One Scanpy image remains for controls and will be removed after archive readback. Raw Matchms evidence remains private. No pipeline promoted. Detailed logs remain in comments.

comment_body:
🤖 **OpenMS checkout recovery is verified.** The original 60-second checkout timed out again. With only checkout's allowance changed to 300 seconds, the same frozen commit completed checkout in 77.899 seconds, with the expected HEAD/tree and no tracked changes. Clone/fetch commands and their limits, pinned controller image, 1 CPU/4 GiB and Git 2.47.3 were held fixed. Both arms used fresh containers/checkouts.

[Acquisition readback](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/875eab80/experiments/29-runtime-limits/openms-checkout-readback-001.json) · [Supervisor cleanup](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/875eab80/experiments/29-runtime-limits/openms-checkout-result-001.json) · [Candidate patch](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/8ae98a2f/experiments/29-runtime-limits/checkout-timeout.patch).

This supports the 60-second checkout limit as a real barrier in this comparison. Baseline-first/shared-cache/network effects remain uncontrolled, but the successful checkout itself exceeded the original limit. No bootstrap, repository installation, PR discovery, task generation or model call followed; no task-recovery claim is made.

The one-attempt job used 0.12592 allocated CPU-hours. Its 9,938-byte archive was read back and all output hashes verified. Both owned containers/checkouts and downloaded tooling were removed with no cleanup errors. #29 now has 1.18825 measured CPU-hours across nine terminal jobs, plus the still-active Scanpy controls and their existing maximum reservation. No new capacity or model spending.
